passages.text: Q: Can’t I just be a good person without any of this? Good conduct is valuable, but conduct completeness means the individual’s continuous expression of realised understanding. MVD pp. 15–16 distinguishes completeness in an individual from completeness in society. A person’s humane participation helps establish and transmit an awakened tradition; it does not require an already completed universal society. The claim is assessed through understanding, fulfilled relationships and continuity of conduct (§1.11.2, §1.15).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: We can now bring constitution, understanding and conduct together through three milestones — T1, T2, and T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: T1 is the constitutional completeness we examined earlier: the immortality of result. A developing atom becomes a sentient unit — jeevan. Its standing changes from physicochemical to sentient before realisation, on what the texts call the delusional plane. In human living, delusion means mistaking the body for the self. In animal living, expression is limited by the bodily medium. The plane name should not turn that limitation into a human error or a psychiatric diagnosis.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: T2 is activity completeness: restfulness of effort. Knowing, believing, recognising and fulfilling become coherent through realisation and resolution. The search arising from body-identification settles into awakened understanding.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: T3 is conduct completeness: destination of motion. That understanding becomes continuous in work, behaviour and participation — authentic conduct as living proof.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: T2 concerns the settlement of understanding; T3 concerns its continuous evidence in conduct. Together they describe awakening within an already complete sentient constitution.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: T1 is completeness of an atom’s constitution. T2 and T3 are not further material stages; they name completeness of activity and conduct in the awakened sentient unit. In one line: the saturated realises the ground it is saturated in.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-20
passages.text: One naming point, since I have just used the words. Physicochemical, delusional, deific, divine — the band across the top of this slide — are what the texts call the four planes. A plane is the developmental standing a thing has reached. It is not a kind of thing, and it is not the same as an order of nature. The next slide sorts that out properly.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-20
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-20
passages.text: “In the sentient atom: Conduct completeness is in the form of destination of motion. Activity completeness is in the form of restfulness of effort. Constitutional completeness (the jeevan atom) is in the form of immortality of result.” — SB, p. 58

passages.heading: primary-text-background-20
passages.text: Both MVD and SB use aacharan purnata for T3; vyavahar purnata appears in neither as the T3 term. Plane table: SB, p. 52. Human types by awakening: MVD, p. 160.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-20
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-20
passages.text: Q: Can a transition reverse? T1 is explicitly irreversible at the atomic level (SB, p. 92). For T2/T3 the texts emphasise directional awakening progression rather than a doctrine of relapse.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-20
passages.text: Q: What distinguishes deific from divine? Deific ≈ T2 (understanding settled); divine ≈ T3 (understanding proven in living proof / pramanikta).

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Four vocabularies now help us distinguish the aspects of order and development we have examined.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: There is one drive: nature saturated in state-complete Omnipresence, oriented toward development and awakening until realisation. Everything on this table is a way of describing where something stands in that drive.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Orders — material, bio, animal, knowledge — say what kind of thing a unit is: its organisation, its essential nature, its innateness. Four orders.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Order and development are described by four terms: existential progression, way of existence, development progression, and awakening progression. The first names the definite order in which the orders become manifest; the second, the conformance by which each order keeps its conduct; the third, physicochemical and atomic development up to T1; the fourth, qualitative development inside a complete sentient unit toward T2 and T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Planes — physicochemical, delusional, deific, divine — say how far something has come. These are the four we just saw across the top of the last slide. Before T1; T1 only; T2; T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: Human types — animalistic, demonic, humane or discerning, deific, divine — say how a human life is oriented. Five of them, and they classify modes of consciousness and conduct. Not biological species. Not social classes. Not castes.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-21
passages.text: The one caution worth stating out loud: an order is not a plane. The knowledge order spans more than one plane — most human beings are in the knowledge order and on the delusional plane at the same time, and there is nothing insulting in that; it just means realisation has not happened yet. T1 separates physicochemical from sentient standing. T2 and T3 are completeness within an awakened sentient unit, and no fifth plane is added beyond them.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: Study §§1.7, 1.11 (the completeness drive), §1.12.1 (terms for order and development), §1.12.2 (four planes, five human types), and the conceptual map’s classification key.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: The four terms for order and development are niyati-kram (existential progression), niyati-vidhi (way of existence), vikas-kram (development progression), and jagriti-kram (awakening progression): MVD, pp. 13–14; study §1.12.1.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: The four planes are physicochemical, delusional, deific, and divine or complete: study §1.12.2. Order vs plane asymmetry: SB, p. 52 — two orders can share one plane; one order can span three planes.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-21
passages.text: The five human types are animalistic-human, demonic-human, humane or discerning human, deific-human, and divine-human: MVD, p. 160; study §1.12.2.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: Why keep four overlapping vocabularies at all? Because collapsing them produces false equations — “animal order = delusional plane = incomplete atom” is the classic one, and every part of it is wrong. Each vocabulary answers a different question, and the drive they describe is single.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: Where do the five human types sit? They mark orientation within human living, distributed across planes (MVD, p. 160) — not a fifth ontology beside coexistence, and not a ranking of persons by birth.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-21
passages.text: Q: Is the delusional plane an insult? No, and it is worth saying so. It is the technical name for sentient standing before realisation: the body taken as the self. It names a condition that awakening addresses, not a defect of character. Note also that an animal’s narrower expression is a limitation of its bodily medium, not the specifically human error of body-identification.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: We can now connect the faculties and harmonies of jeevan with values fulfilled in relationships.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: A relationship carries definite expectations towards completeness — parent and child, for example. In a contact, or sampark, the particular exchange is voluntarily undertaken, as when neighbours agree to share the upkeep of a wall. Both remain answerable to justice and humane conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: The thirty values belong to five families. Four jeevan values are the harmonies we have examined: happiness, peace, contentment and bliss. Six human values are the humane qualities of fortitude, courage, generosity, kindness, grace and compassion. Nine established values include trust, respect, affection and care. Nine expressed values are their corresponding expressions in conduct. The two object values are usefulness and art value — the meaningful convenience and beauty that enhance usefulness.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: The family tells us what evaluative role a value fulfils. The faculty tells us where the activity is borne in jeevan. The four harmonies are borne at mun, vritti, chitta and buddhi. The nine established values are borne three each at chitta, vritti and mun, with their corresponding expressions. Object values concern the useful material means through which work and bodily needs are supported.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Bearing a value and fulfilling it in a relationship are distinct. A person may intend to care for an ill parent, but care becomes effective through recognising the parent’s needs, arranging suitable help, and checking the result. A useful object can support that care; attention, trust and respect concern how the people relate.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-22
passages.text: Knowing and believing therefore guide recognising and fulfilling. Established values become evident as relationships are fulfilled; expressed values carry them into conduct. The next slide examines how fulfilment is evaluated.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: “Every entity of nature recognises another; that is why it fulfils…” — JV, p. 69

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: Relationship / contact definitions: MVD, pp. 61–62. Values and mutuality: SB, pp. 50, 53, 61; MVD, p. 27. Motherly care example: JV, pp. 137–138.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: The thirty-value enumeration is explicit in Paribhasha Samhita pp. 151, 154; definitions and connections are developed across several passages. Manav Abhyas Darshan, native-reader p. 30, gives the principal nine established values and their paired expressions. The English translation of MVD uses civic values for shishta-mulya; this companion treats them as the expressed pair of the established values. See the study’s §1.13.1 and Axiology §1.3.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-22
passages.text: Value families and their faculty locations: study §1.13.1; MVD pp. 328–348; AVD pp. 91–94. The family identifies evaluative role, while the faculty identifies the bearer of the activity. The caregiver illustration follows study §1.13.3. Bearing values and fulfilling relationships remain distinct (JV p. 55).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-22
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-22
passages.text: Q: Aren’t values subjective? In MD, essentiality is value — reciprocated and mutually recognised in mutuality. Cultures differ in recognition and evaluation, not in the underlying essentiality.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-22
passages.text: Q: Do relationships exist below the human order? Yes — even physicochemical components recognise and fulfil one another (SB, p. 123). Below the knowledge order, fulfilment is definite; at the human order it must be achieved through the knowing–believing–recognising–fulfilling chain.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: We introduced six perspectives when examining restricted deliberation. Here they guide the evaluation of living: pleasant–unpleasant, healthy–unhealthy, profit–loss, justice–injustice, dharma–adharma, and truth–untruth.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: The first three concern sensation, the body, and material production or exchange. The final three concern relationship, resolved thought and existence as coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Justice evaluates behaviour. As a completed relational activity, it means recognising relationships, fulfilling values, evaluating the fulfilment, and achieving mutual satisfaction. Trust or care contributes to justice when it is actually fulfilled in the relationship.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Dharma as an evaluative perspective concerns whether thought and policy support resolution and overall orderliness. This differs from unit dharma, the inseparable innateness introduced earlier. Truth concerns the coexistence that is understood through realisation.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: The text connects these levels in a graduated chain: rule is justice, justice is dharma, dharma is truth, and truth is coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-23
passages.text: Pleasure, health and material benefit remain legitimate in their domains. Humane evaluation places them under justice, resolved thought and truth, so that the useful means of living serve fulfilled relationships and the human goal.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-23
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-23
passages.text: KD, pp. 10, 13, 60, 86; study §§1.13.2–1.13.3. Rule is justice, justice is dharma, dharma is truth, and truth is coexistence — KD p. 13 (working-English paraphrase). MVD, p. 67 (six perspectives); MVD, p. 137 (justice regulates behaviour, dharma disciplines thought, realisation only through truth); MVD, p. 311 (justice as recognising relationships, fulfilling values, evaluating, mutual satisfaction). JV, pp. 138–139 (deliberation bases).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-23
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-23
passages.text: Q: Are pleasure, health, and profit condemned? No — legitimate in their domain; awakening changes the organising refuge.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-23
passages.text: Q: How does this relate to courts? Distinguish inherent regulation, justice as relational closure, and statutory law. Statute can be legal and unjust.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: This brings the account of knowing together: what must be understood, and how understanding deepens within jeevan.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: On the left: what must be understood as mutual context widens. Form is real structure encountered in mutual facing. Capacities show as effects between units. Essential nature needs state, order, and context. Innateness is evidenced in whole-order fulfilment. Relationships are shared expectations weighed by justice, dharma, and truth. At the top is coexistence itself — not another observed detail, but the aim of knowing.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: On the right: how knowing happens within the sentient unit. Mun tastes and selects. Vritti deliberates. Chitta contemplates and directly apprehends. Buddhi comprehends and resolves. Atma realises in truth. Happiness, peace, contentment, and bliss name harmonies between paired faculties. Realisation at atma is named ultimate bliss.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-24
passages.text: Every unit is already manifest with all four aspects. The left-hand steps describe widening human understanding of that unit; they do not describe successive additions to its image. Inward reflection deepens knowing, and projection makes understanding evident through conduct. Bliss names the harmony of buddhi and atma; coexistence realised at atma is ultimate bliss.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-24
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-24
passages.text: JV, p. 120 (triad epistemic bases); JV, p. 121; SB, p. 50 (ultimate dharma); JV, p. 120 (understanding of existence, jeevan, and humane conduct); MVD, pp. 78, 101, 137; JV, p. 61; study §§1.3, 1.8–1.9, 1.13–1.14.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-24
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-24
passages.text: Q: Why is dharma on the top rung when atma is at the centre of the atom diagram? Different geometries: atom diagram is structural (inward = deeper); ladder is epistemic (higher = wider context needed). All four aspects are equally present in every unit.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-24
passages.text: Q: Is this ladder stated verbatim in the texts? The ladder is an analytical arrangement of the definitions and their contexts, as explained in the study. All four aspects belong to the manifest unit. Imaging supplies a basis of recognition, while human understanding develops through jeevan’s knowing activities; the rungs should not be taught as a source-enumerated sequence of images.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: This is where the developmental drive comes to rest: realisation in coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Realisation settles jeevan’s search arising from delusion. The awakened sentient unit understands the coexistence in which it has always existed and evidences that understanding through fulfilled relationships and humane conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Realisation at atma is named ultimate bliss. Bliss names the harmony of buddhi and atma. What is known is existence as coexistence: nature saturated in Omnipresence. Understanding becomes evident as authenticity in work, behaviour, and participation. The next slide examines how it is presented, communicated, and expressed.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-25
passages.text: Three roles stay distinct: the sentient unit remains the knower; existence as coexistence remains the known; knowledge becomes evident as authentic conduct. Its threefold content is the holistic view of coexistence, knowledge of jeevan, and knowledge of humane conduct. They become coherent without becoming identical. The individual knower is not dissolved into a single universal Self.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: “The goal of development is for nature, saturated in Omnipotence, to be realised in Omnipotence…” — SB, p. 81

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: SB, p. 116 and MVD, p. 126 (threefold knowledge); KD §§3.17–3.18 (knowledge, knower, and known); MVD, pp. 14–15, 286–287. Study §1.14.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-25
passages.text: MVD pp. 100–101 distinguishes ultimate bliss at atma; MVD p. 328 connects realisation-based expression, communication, and exposition with ultimate bliss. Study §§1.9 and 1.14 preserves both this placement and bliss as buddhi–atma harmony.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-25
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-25
passages.text: Q: If satta is Knowledge, doesn’t it know everything? No — gyan as satta names intelligibility, not cognition. The knowing act belongs only to jeevan.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-25
passages.text: Q: How is this different from moksha as merger? MD denies merger into a single Self. Realisation evidences coexistence; individuality of jeevan remains ontologically real.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Every unit is prakashman, manifest through its form, properties, essential nature and dharma. Presentation, communication and expression describe this participation throughout nature. In sentient jeevan, manifestness includes its active faculties and the capacities it expresses through the body. Humans already communicate and express their capacities during awakening progression. With awakening, these activities carry realised understanding into meaningful presentation, communication and conduct. The three definitions here describe that fuller human fulfilment.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Presentation, prakashan, makes actuality evident through an accomplished and meaningful form. Something understood becomes available for another to attend to.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Communication, sampreshana, indicates completeness. The definition names constitutional completeness, activity completeness and conduct completeness. In human communication, words direct attention to the activity of units and its inherent meaning, serving understanding and enabling another to understand.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Expression, abhivyakti, is the mental, verbal and bodily activity through which one’s existence is evidenced for all-round resolution, called abhyudaya. Understanding becomes evident in speech, work and humane behaviour.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: Art, kala, is skilful expressive activity: it makes qualities evident and expression meaningful, joining usefulness with beauty. Art value, kala-mulya, is the value realised in an object when meaningful convenience and beauty enhance its usefulness. A well-made object can evidence that value; a clear explanation can evidence art in making understanding intelligible.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-26
passages.text: These are connected, overlapping aspects of sentient manifestation. Their fulfilment in awakened human living carries realised understanding through the body into conduct and the humane tradition.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: The general scope is unit expression according to state, motion, developmental plane, and order (SB p. 179), and all units’ expressions as activity saturated in Omnipresence (MVD p. 109). The sentient connection is explicit in SB pp. 52, 63, 66, 90–92: jeevan manifests through the body, its faculties are active and manifest, and communication/expression during awakening progression is itself a meaning of prakashmanata (p. 66). The fuller human definitions are PS p. 119 for prakashan, p. 206 for sampreshana, and p. 22 for abhivyakti. The definition of abhivyakti itself includes prakashan and the participation of hope, thought, desire, resolve, experience, and bodily activity.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: MVD pp. 109–110 connects form activity, word activity, inherent meaning, and communication as understanding and enabling understanding. MVD p. 328 brings realisation-based expression, communication, and exposition together under ultimate bliss. These connections support a coherent account without assigning each term exclusively to one faculty pair.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-26
passages.text: PS p. 56 defines kala through making qualities evident and expression meaningful, and the joint accomplishment of usefulness and beauty. Its object-value application, kala-mulya, concerns enhancing usefulness; the general definition also concerns communication and conduct. All PS page numbers are printed pages in the edition identified at the start of this companion. Study §1.14 and Editorial Notes give the connected reading and contextual qualifications.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Does sentient expression begin only after awakening? SB p. 66 explicitly describes communication and expression during awakening progression as prakashmanata. Awakening brings their fulfilment as realised understanding and humane conduct. SB p. 179 also preserves the wider use of expression vocabulary across all four orders.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Does each term add a new layer to the unit’s image? The sources do not establish three successive layers or an exhaustive partition of manifestness. The terms overlap, and abhivyakti’s definition includes prakashan. Their human definitions specify meaningful presentation, indication of completeness, and expression for all-round resolution.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Can we map presentation to vritti–chitta, communication to chitta–buddhi, and expression to buddhi–atma? The reviewed definitions do not establish that exclusive assignment. MVD p. 328 uses all three together for realisation-based ultimate bliss, and abhivyakti involves the full activity of jeevan through the body. The faculty harmonies on slide 17 remain distinct definitions.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-26
passages.text: Q: Does kala mean decoration? Its definition joins usefulness and beauty and makes expression meaningful. A clear explanation or accomplished piece of work can evidence it. Object art value is one application of this broader account.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Conduct completeness is realised understanding expressed continuously by the individual. Humane participation and education transmit it through an awakened tradition. Individual completeness contributes to social completeness; it does not wait for the entire society to be complete.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Effort settled in realisation is T2. Understanding proven in conduct is T3.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Four goals at four levels: resolution in every person; prosperity in every family; fearlessness — trust — in society; coexistence with all of nature.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: Five social systems carry that continuity: education and formative culture; justice and preservation; health and restraint; production and work; exchange and storage. These differ from the four dimensions of a person’s living — realisation, thought, behaviour and work.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: And here is where the other half of the composition slide returns. Families and societies are not a further compositional tier — you cannot get a humane society by stacking bodies the way you stack molecules. They are relational achievements: they persist humanely while relationships are recognised, values fulfilled, evaluation completed, and mutual satisfaction achieved. Fear, force, or extraction can hold a group together for a while; on this account they do not make it an orderly society.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-27
passages.text: MD connects this social aim with human dharma as happiness, values fulfilled in relationships, and understanding expressed in conduct. Nature is oriented towards development and realisation; an awakened human tradition requires people to understand, practise, and transmit that understanding. The ontology gives this participation a purpose without making humane institutions automatic.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-27
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-27
passages.text: JV, PDF p. 61; MVD, pp. 13–16; SB, pp. 51, 81, 91. Individual and social completeness are distinguished in MVD pp. 15–16. Five social systems: study §1.15 and governance-related works in the series. SB on operating scale of self-sustaining systems (100–200 families) if useful for Q&A.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-27
passages.text: Human assemblies as achieved rather than chemically definite: study §1.13.3; MVD, p. 42; SB, p. 14 (persist or decline). This is the counterpart of slide 13 — physical composition (§1.5) was delivered there, human assemblies (§1.13.3) here.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-27
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-27
passages.text: Q: Isn’t ‘producing more than needed’ just growth ideology? No — samridhi is felt sufficiency with proper utilisation, opposed to hoarding (AVD).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-27
passages.text: Q: How does family-scale vision reach society? Through coordinated participation in recognised relationships, expressed institutionally across the five social systems. Social continuity requires continued fulfilment; it is not a chemical composition of persons.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: The account we have examined uses several modes of inquiry and evidence. Each answers a different question.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Logical exposition tests whether definitions and relationships form a coherent account. Study and self-examination test whether the proposal and the activities of knowing can be understood and recognised.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Experiment and practice in work and behaviour test whether understanding regulates action. Conduct-evidence makes relational consequences — fulfilled values, mutual satisfaction and participation — visible to others.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: Realisation is Madhyasth Darshan’s claimed completion of knowing coexistence, jeevan and humane conduct. Its status as first-person completion differs from publicly measurable physical evidence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: The sentience threshold, the jeevan–body interface, and post-body reassociation raise physical questions. No accepted measurement currently identifies them. The survival and reassociation account introduced with the joint form remains a claim to examine under that further standard.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-28
passages.text: These methods can support one another while retaining their different scope. Evidence of humane conduct does not by itself identify the sentient atom, just as internal coherence alone does not establish that a physical claim is true.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-28
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-28
passages.text: Study §1.16. Staged method from MVD, p. 88 and SB, p. 44: study → experiment and practice → realisation with evidence. Open problems: study §§6.1–6.2.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-28
passages.text: T1 is introduced on slide 14. The joint form, interface, post-body persistence and later reassociation are introduced on slide 15. The method slide distinguishes their physical evidential questions from the first-person and conduct-based methods described in study §1.16.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-28
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-28
passages.text: Q: Has any of this been proven scientifically? Be precise: internal coherence and conceptual consonance are not instrument confirmation of T1 or post-body continuity. Use “consonant with,” never “supported by,” without evidence.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-28
passages.text: Q: Then why present it? Because ontology can still be examined for definitions, entailments, and lived testability — and because refusing to overclaim is part of the method.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Delivering the slide

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Let us close the loop on the six questions.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: What is existence? Eternal coexistence: countless units saturated in all-pervasive Omnipresence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: What exists? Root atomic units; composite units and bodies; body–sentient-unit joint forms; and relational human assemblies — all saturated in the ground.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Does existence begin or end? No. Existence is perpetual. Configurations form, transform, and decompose.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: What is the self? The constitutionally complete sentient unit working through the body.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: Is the world real? Yes. Units, mutual relationships, and definite material fulfilment are real within perpetual coexistence.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: How is it known? Through logical exposition, study and self-examination, practice, realisation, and conduct-evidence — without conflating those with instrument measurement of the sentience threshold. The lived test is evidence in humane conduct.

passages.heading: delivering-the-slide-29
passages.text: If we continue later, the natural next step is comparison with other traditions and with science — including open problems this study names for Madhyasth Darshan itself. Thank you.

passages.heading: primary-text-background-29
passages.text: Primary-text background

passages.heading: primary-text-background-29
passages.text: Study §1.16 table. Staged method: MVD, p. 88; SB, p. 44. Open problems: §§6.1–6.2 (latency reading, conservation-to-immortality inference, jeevan–body interaction, operationalization of T1, niyati-kram vs evolution).

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-29
passages.text: Likely questions from the audience

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-29
passages.text: Q: Where should someone start? Follow the staging: study (JV, then SB/MVD with this paper as map) → experiment and practice in living → let realisation and conduct be the test. Jeevan Vidya shivirs follow this format.

passages.heading: likely-questions-from-the-audience-29
passages.text: Q: What’s the single takeaway? Existence is coexistence: a changeless, actionless ground and countless real units, saturated together — and because complementarity and value are built into that togetherness, human fulfilment is recognising and fulfilling relationships, evidenced in conduct. Resolution = happiness.
